articles.title: GTA 6 Has A Metacritic Score So High It’s Only Happened Once Before
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has officially launched, and unsurprisingly, it's earning rave reviews. It's arriving hot on the heels of several critically acclaimed games this year, but does it have enough momentum to knock the current best-reviewed game of the year, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time…
body: When Ocarina of Time launched in early November, it quickly shot to the top of the Metacritic charts, earning a metascore of 96 from GameSpot's sister site. That score came from 128 reviews, and Metacritic rates it as "Universal Acclaim" on its scale. For GTA 6, the game is sitting on a review aggregate of 99 from 98 reviews at the time of writing, with just a single point keeping it away from a perfect score. One thing to note is that Ocarina of Time had more reviews than GTA 6, which affects the review weighting, but overall, both games drew from a broad pool of outlets worldwide.

Don't feel too bad for Ocarina of Time losing its crown, because the only thing better than critical success is commercial success. The remake has sold more than 5 million copies globally in its first four days, and those numbers will keep growing as we enter the festive season. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick recently reacted to the game's release, saying it's "terrific" and that Nintendo has every right to be proud of it.

articles.title: GTA 6 is Now The Joint-Highest Rated Game of All Time
articles.summary: GTA 6 has become the joint-highest rated game of all time, following the widespread publication of reviews in the past hour. Rockstar's masterpiece currently sits with an all-time best score of 99 on Metacritic, an honor shared only with Nintendo's original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time…
body: While both the N64 version of Ocarina and GTA 6 share a 99 average, GTA 6 has impressively managed to pull this off with more than six times' the number of reviews — over 120 at the time of writing, with over 100 of those listed with a perfect score. And while it's possible GTA 6's ranking could still slip down a point as more reviews are published, it would still be the best-rated game in nearly three decades.

Few others titles released in the recent memory have come anywhere close to this — though if you head back to the last console generation, Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Super Mario Odyssey both managed a 97 average, a standing they share with Rockstar's own Red Dead Redemption 2.

IGN's GTA 6 review is of course now live, and also returned a perfect 10/10 score. We described it as "exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered," as well as "unprecedented, unbelievable and unmissable."

articles.title: KFC Australia Is Holding a Fake Funeral for Ann Alibi So You Can Take the Day Off for GTA 6
articles.summary: When famous people die, they break attendance records for funerals all the time. I have a feeling the upcoming funeral for the definitely real Ann Alibi might blow those attendance numbers out of the water though. KFC Australia is hosting a fake funeral so players can book work off for GTA 6.
body: “Ann Alibi was always there for us. Now you can be there for her,” the company said in an Instagram post.
“Join us Thursday 19 November for a funeral at KFC ROBINA, QLD, streamed live on Instagram from 11am AEDT. Any resemblance to a certain launch date is purely coincidental.”

The post is currently at 5.5k likes, but if it reaches 6k the company will offer free delivery throughout Australia for GTA 6 launch day. If you can’t get to Australia for a fake funeral and some free chicken, KFC plans to livestream the event. The service includes "a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest."
According to statistics, GTA 6 has already caused a 17% spike in time off requests at work this week as hype hits fever pitch for the game’s long-awaited launch.

articles.title: GTA 6 Has A Clever PS5 DualSense Trick For Keeping You Under The Speed Limit
articles.summary: While the urge to be an absolute menace in Grand Theft Auto 6 is strong, nothing stops you from playing as a law-abiding citizen who sticks to the speed limit between missions.
body: On PS5, GTA 6 players can keep their vehicle from going over the speed limit, as the adaptive triggers provide resistance when you get close to the legal limit. That doesn't mean that you can't break past that barrier, but the adaptive triggers will help you match traffic speed most of the time and stick to legal restrictions. That essentially makes it easier to control your vehicle and gives your index fingers a sense of how hard to press the triggers--useful when you're trying to avoid dinging your car by finding that sweet spot.

This is just one of several vehicle-specific features in GTA 6, as the game borrows a few ideas from modern-day open-world games and puts its own spin on it. For example, you can summon your car via a smartphone app, which involves a Scooter Bros. employee appearing at your location, delivering your ride, and then disappearing into the sunset with the little two-wheeled ride they stashed in your trunk.

articles.title: GTA 6 Xbox Series S Performance: How Does the Weakest Console Handle the Biggest Game of All Time?
articles.summary: GTA 6 is finally here, and one of the biggest questions heading up to launch is how well the Xbox Series S would handle the game – well, I've finally had the chance to play the game on the tiny Xbox.
body: Rockstar announced a couple weeks ago that all versions of GTA 6 would be 'targeting' 30 fps, and while it's disappointing that even the PS5 Pro won't be able to hit 60 fps, that performance is about what I expected from the Xbox Series S. And while I wait for my framerate analysis to stop running on my first clip of the game, the Xbox Series S version actually seems pretty decent, all things considered.

The Xbox Series S obviously doesn't have the same graphics treats that the PS5 Pro version of the game has, but even without the ray traced shadows and the PSSR, the game holds up well on the 1440p machine. Character models are still extremely detailed, and even has some decent subsurface scattering and the environments are incredibly beautiful, no doubt learning from Rockstar's time with Red Dead Redemption 2.

articles.summary: It’s finally here. GTA 6 is now available to play for both physical and virtual residents of New Zealand, and we’ve got a brand new slice of gameplay for you to check out.

You’ll get to check out just how stupidly gorgeous that water looks, a blend of both stealth takedowns and loud gunplay action, as well as some of that trademark Rockstar humour. Enjoy!

articles.title: GTA 6 Gym Workouts Have A Useful Trick That Saves You A Lot Of Time
articles.summary: You won't get muscles in real life without putting in some work, but fortunately, leveling up your pectorals in Grand Theft Auto 6 is much less strenuous. The only cardio you'll need to do is a series of finger movements on your controller, but admittedly, getting either of the game's protagonists…
body: Essentially, all you need to do in GTA 6 is make sure you're going to the gym as a couple. If you only focus on Jason or Lucia for a workout, then they'll gradually gain muscle and tone up on their own. But if you go as a pair, it doesn't matter who you work out with; both characters will gain and progress on their path toward becoming absolute units.
That makes for a quick way to bulk up, though we still need to talk about Jason's gym etiquette.

This isn't the first time GTA has introduced gym gameplay mechanics to keep your protagonist in shape; back in GTA: San Andreas, players could frequent locations across the map and work on CJ's appearance. Not only could he increase his muscle mass and stamina by pumping iron, but CJ could also learn new fighting styles from trainers along the way. Working out in GTA 6 also has benefits, as lifting weights can improve overall health, while cardio activities like running and biking improve stamina.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Exploit Lands Streamers In Hot Water After Farming Thousands Of Gold
articles.summary: A lucrative World of Warcraft: Forever dungeon-farming exploit that netted some players hundreds of gold per hour has been hotfixed, and Blizzard is taking action against accounts that (temporarily) walked away with thousands in loot.
body: For the dedicated few who have already reached max level in the new version of Blizzard's MMORPG, a new endgame dungeon, Blackmaw Hold, proved to be quite lucrative. In the dungeon, a room with 30 non-elite enemies proved to be the perfect spot for area-of-effect gold farming, since it's easy to access.

As detailed by Wowhead, the farm was as simple as running to the room in question, killing all the mobs, looting them, resetting the dungeon, and repeating. Not only did the enemies drop anywhere from 25 to 50 silver each, but they also dropped items that could be sold either to a vendor or on the auction house for even more profit.

And some players, including prominent streamers, did just that during Forever's second weekend. One streamer, Ziqo, who was previously in hot water for accepting illegal gold during the game's beta, revealed he made 4,000 gold from the farm. On stream, Ziqo named other streamers who did the same and said his only regret was choosing to sleep for four hours instead of farming longer.

articles.title: Clair Obscur's narrative lead has left developer Sandfall Interactive after "wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition"
articles.summary: Last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year.
body: "No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a new generation of video game narrative designers.

"One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors."

articles.title: GTA 6 Hits 99 on Metacritic, Crowned Best Game Ever in Wave of Rave Reviews
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has displaced the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the best video game of all time according to review aggregation site Metacritic. Its Metascore of 99 matches Nintendo's 1998 masterpiece, but is presumably a few decimal points higher behind the scenes.
body: It is rated even more highly than Rockstar's last two monoliths, Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, which both earned Metascores of 97. It's a similar story on OpenCritic, where GTA 6 has a rating of 98.
Reviewers are universally bowled over by the scale, ambition, and artistry of Rockstar Games' magnum opus, which they have hailed in a near-unbroken string of five-star, 10/10 reviews.

IGN's Luke Reilly called GTA 6 "one of the most impressive games ever made" in his 10/10 review, and called it "Unprecedented. Unbelievable. Unmissable." Like many reviewers, Reilly noted how the latest GTA had inherited the sophistication and maturity of Red Dead Redemption 2 as well as the anarchic spirit of its predecessors. "As optimistic as I was about a new GTA built in the wake of everything Rockstar learnt from the majestic Red Dead Redemption 2, I was simply not ready for just how much richer, deeper, and more satisfying Grand Theft Auto 6 has proven to be," Reilly wrote.

articles.title: 20 Years Later, Paramount's Serial Killer Series Officially Breaks a Weird TV Record
articles.summary: Gabriel Luna has a rule: He doesn't play villains unless it's opposite "the greatest action hero who's ever lived," aka Arnold Schwarzenegger. "I have an I only play heroes kind of mindset," the actor tells Polygon.
body: This isn't just an aspirational goal. It's already happened twice. Luna portrayed Rev-9, an advanced killer robot in Terminator: Dark Fate, and he was an evil arms dealer in the Netflix series FUBAR, both of which starred Schwarzenegger. But in 2026, Luna broke his own rule to take on a very different kind of role: a serial killer.

Luna plays Ray Ballard, aka the Sleepy-Eyed Killer, across two episodes of Dexter: Resurrection season 2. It's a role he was drawn to because of the complex psychology at work within the character, who stalks and kills his victims while they sleep.
"I was fascinated by the psychological warfare he plays with them as he does these home invasions and enters the home for weeks and weeks before he ever culminates the kill," Luna says.
Speaking to Polygon, the Last of Us star goes deep into the backstory he invented for the Sleepy-Eyed Killer and the surprising record he broke while shooting his most pivotal scene.

articles.title: Slay the Spire 2 is one of this year's best selling games despite only being available on PC, and its players are "obsessed"
articles.summary: One million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March.
body: That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.

Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox. That is notable, as the game is only out on Steam, meaning it has sold enough copies to outpace games on platforms it's not even available on.

We already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. It quickly became March's top-selling game on Steam, beating blockbuster competition in Crimson Desert and Resident Evil Requiem. Slay the Spire 2, alongside other indie titles such as Meccha Chameleon, have helped Steam deliver another record year of revenue.

It was such a hit, even, that other indie developers felt it negatively impacted sales of their own games. Mewgenics maker Edmund McMillen recently told Eurogamer "it sucked everybody out". "The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over," McMillen said.

articles.title: GTA 6 Officially Launches, Spoiler Warning Issued for Players Still Waiting
articles.summary: After many long years of waiting and a handful of delays, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 will finally be released on Thursday, Nov. 19. For some players, it's out right now.
body: GTA 6 has a rolling midnight launch schedule, meaning it's available to play at 12 a.m. your local time on Nov. 19. Due to the power of time zones and a round Earth, midnight local time on Nov. 19 arrives in some territories while it's still Nov. 18 in others. New Zealanders will get first access as GTA 6 gradually unlocks around the world.

The internet is beholden to no time zone. Until it's midnight Nov. 19 in your time zone, you'll have to be aware that spoilers will naturally flood social media and other sites. Depending on where they live, players in New Zealand and elsewhere will have multiple hours to play GTA 6 while the timer on their PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X is still counting down. For example, midnight in New Zealand on Nov. 19 is 6 a.m. EST on Nov. 18 on the east coast of the United States. U.S.-based players will have to be careful to avoid spoilers for essentially the whole day on Wednesday.

articles.title: The GTA 6 Review
articles.summary: When we first meet the co-star of Grand Theft Auto 6, she’s scraping the bottom of the cultural barrel. She’s a lowly street rat. The only person who seems to give a damn about her is Jason Duval, another small-time crook who connects with her during a star-crossed carjacking turned meet-cute.
body: Who gets to break the rules in America? A cryptobro living off of financial scams. A girlboss CEO who turns feminine vulnerability into a pyramid scheme. A cop who shoots a civilian in the face and walks away scot-free. It’s an exclusive club of societally acceptable grifters and killers, and Lucia Caminos’ name isn’t on the VIP list.
When Lucia is finally set free, it’s not because society has decided that this financially desperate Latina has earned a second chance. It’s because of an overcrowding crisis at the jail.

In a sprawling satirical sandbox filled with loudmouth radio DJs and over-the-top conservative cartoons, it’s the sharpest stab GTA 6 lands on American culture. Justice is big business in the Florida-inspired state of Leonida, and people like Lucia are products to be cycled in and out of a flawed system. All the while, the real criminal masterminds of Leonida trash their penthouses into the wee morning hours.

articles.title: "We'd love to have you" - New Zealand's tourist board gives a nod to those hopping timezones to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early
articles.summary: New Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early.
body: "One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first."

For those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result.

Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 New Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it.

videos.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) Review
videos.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 reviewed by Luke Reilly on PlayStation 5. Also available on Xbox Series X|S.
body: "As optimistic as I was about a new GTA built in the wake of everything Rockstar learnt from the majestic Red Dead Redemption 2, I was simply not ready for just how much richer, deeper, and more satisfying Grand Theft Auto 6 has proven to be. After three weeks and over 120 hours playing it, I’m still hopelessly hooked, absorbing the world at walking speed like a tourist in a new town. I’m dazed by just how consistently I find myself noticing a new animation, unique pedestrian, or standout vehicle. I am completely enamoured with its series-best car handling and weaving through the realistically dense traffic. I am smitten with its spark-filled shootouts, potent explosions, and the brutal consequences of high-calibre exchanges. I am floored at how outright gorgeous the entire map is from any distance, and I am utterly gobsmacked at how beautifully lit it is at all times – especially dawn, dusk, and the dead of night. Exquisitely detailed, endlessly experimentable, and uncompromisingly engineered, GTA 6 has not stopped astonishing me since I started it. I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."
points: Grand Theft Auto 6 reviewed by Luke Reilly on PlayStation 5.

points: While this may not be the very first minutes of Rockstar’s latest Grand Theft Auto, it is taken from the first proper mission of the game, which takes place after a short prologue.
